goal: Create a polished, responsive single-page decision board where a small team can add options, score each option from 1 to 5, immediately see the current leader, retain the board after a page reload, and clear the board safely.
constraints: No server-side application data dependency in the generated product; use browser-local persistence.
Keyboard-accessible controls and readable responsive layout.
No external assets, libraries, network calls, placeholder copy, or unfinished controls.
The interface should feel presentation-ready rather than like a developer prototype.
acceptance_criteria: A user can add at least three named options and each option appears on the board.
A user can set or change a 1-to-5 score for every option and the displayed leader updates immediately with deterministic tie handling.
Reloading the page preserves options and scores in browser-local storage.
Clearing the board requires confirmation and returns to an informative empty state.
The complete primary journey works at desktop and narrow mobile viewport sizes with no console errors.
